suggestions.title: 1. Your MDMA section: do women get a sentence?
suggestions.whose: his own: his MDMA: Magnesium Alarm paragraph (round 42), and his sentence from his QUIZ-3 answer of round 51
suggestions.question:
You wrote that GPT found other reviews give men and women the same risk, and you'd cut my sentence, or use yours: "Women are most at risk of this, based on results we have from one study done at raves, where sodium was low in 1/4 women vs only 3% of men."
What I found: in a controlled study where people took MDMA and drank water, women's sodium did not drop more than men's ([Baggott 2016](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4923534/)). Outside the lab it goes the other way: among MDMA cases reported to California's poison control, women had four times the odds of low sodium and higher odds of a coma from it ([Rosenson 2007](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17084942)), and most of the severe and fatal cases in the reports are young women.
a) Your sentence, after "so have them sip an electrolyte drink when they're thirsty instead", with the poison control numbers added as what it rests on.
b) Leave it out.
If (a), I'll write it from your sentence and check it before it goes in.
suggestions.why: it is your paragraph, and you leaned toward cutting it before seeing the poison control numbers
suggestions.stays: your paragraph as it is, with no sentence on women
suggestions.advice_note: a: the poison control numbers are about real cases, which is what a reader at a festival faces

suggestions.title: 2. Your MDMA section: why not to dance
suggestions.whose: his own: his MDMA-SODIUM answer of round 51, with the line it put in his MDMA paragraph
suggestions.question:
Your paragraph now says: "While it's natural to want to dance on MDMA, I'd tell everyone not to dance at all, since dancing makes the heat and the sweat that drain their salt." You also wrote: "real mdma doesn't give you any energy to dance so i'm highly suspicious that contains amphetamines or it's not real mdma maybe 6apb".
What I found: in controlled studies of pure MDMA, people's ratings of their energy go up with the dose ([Kolbrich 2008](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2587205)), and MDMA shows "some effects commonly associated with stimulant drugs" ([Harris 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12172693/)). So I left your reason about the pills out of the guide for now.
a) Keep the line as it is, with the heat and the sweat as the reason.
b) Add your suspicion as yours, for example: "In my experience pure MDMA doesn't make me want to dance, so a pill that does may have something else in it." I'd check it before it goes in.
c) Something else: say it in the box.
suggestions.why: it is your belief, and the studies I found say pure MDMA does raise energy, so it is your call how to say it
suggestions.advice_note: a, or b said as your own experience
